'''''Rapistrum rugosum''''' is a species of flowering plant in the [[Brassicaceae|mustard family]]<ref>{{PLANTS|id=RARU|taxon=Rapistrum rugosum|accessdate=18 October 2015}}</ref> commonly known as '''bastard cabbage<ref name="Texas-Invasives" />''' or '''annual bastard cabbage''',<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rapistrum rugosum (annual bastard-cabbage) |url=https://gobotany.nativeplanttrust.org/species/rapistrum/rugosum/ |access-date=2024-09-12 |website=Go Botany |publisher=Native Plant Trust}}</ref> as well as "common giant mustard", "turnipweed", "ball mustard", "wild turnip", "wild rape", or "tall mustard-weed".<ref name="Texas-Invasives">{{Cite web |title=Rapistrum rugosum |url=https://www.texasinvasives.org/plant_database/detail.php?symbol=RARU |access-date=2024-09-12 |website=Texas Invasives}}</ref> It is native to parts of [[Eurasia]] and [[Africa]],<ref name="Plants-of-the-World-Online">{{Cite web |title=Rapistrum rugosum (L.) All. |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:1061021-2 |access-date=2024-09-28 |website=[[Plants of the World Online]] |publisher=[[Kew Science]] |language=en}}</ref> but is present throughout the world as an [[introduced species]] and a common [[weed]].<ref name="Plants-of-the-World-Online" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Garcia |first=Ariana |title=Beware the mighty 'Bastard cabbage' pushing out Texas' bluebonnets |url=https://www.chron.com/life/wildlife/article/texas-bluebonnets-bastard-cabbage-19363013.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250613125107/https://www.chron.com/life/wildlife/article/texas-bluebonnets-bastard-cabbage-19363013.php |archive-date=2025-06-13 |access-date=2025-10-14 |work=Chron |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Plant Conservation Alliance's Alien Plant Working Group |title=Fact Sheet: Annual Bastard-Cabbage |url=https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/GOVPUB-I53-PURL-gpo84600/pdf/GOVPUB-I53-PURL-gpo84600.pdf+ |website=Plant Conservation Alliance}}</ref>  It is an [[invasive species]] in many areas. It is an annual herb producing an erect stem reaching up to about a meter tall. The leaves are variable in shape and size and the proximal blades are generally cut into lobes or divided into leaflets. The herbage is coated in rough hairs. The [[inflorescence]] is a [[raceme]] of flowers with dark-veined yellow petals that are each under a centimeter long. The fruit is a knoblike spherical ribbed [[silique]] borne on a long [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicel]] with a widened area where it joins the fruit.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gobotany.nativeplanttrust.org/species/rapistrum/rugosum/|title = Rapistrum rugosum (Annual bastard-cabbage): Go Botany}}</ref> It grows mainly in temperate areas.<ref name="Plants-of-the-World-Online" /> It is used as animal food, as a poison, for medicine, and for food.<ref name="Plants-of-the-World-Online" />
